{{Short description|Space where open mapping and closed graph theorems hold}}
In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[functional analysis]], a '''webbed space''' is a [[topological vector space]] designed with the goal of allowing the results of the [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]] and the [[Closed graph theorem (functional analysis)|closed graph theorem]] to hold for a wider class of [[linear map]]s whose codomains are webbed spaces. A space is called webbed if there exists a collection of [[Set (mathematics)|set]]s, called a ''web'' that satisfies certain properties. Webs were first investigated by de Wilde.

==Web==

Let <math>X</math> be a [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[Locally convex topological vector space|locally convex]] [[topological vector space]]. A '''{{em|{{visible anchor|web}}}}''' is a stratified collection of [[Absolutely convex set|disk]]s satisfying the following absorbency and convergence requirements.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=470−471}} 
# '''Stratum 1''': The first stratum must consist of a sequence <math>D_{1}, D_{2}, D_{3}, \ldots</math> of [[Absolutely convex set|disk]]s in <math>X</math> such that their union <math>\bigcup_{i \in \N} D_i</math> [[Absorbing set|absorbs]] <math>X.</math> 
# '''Stratum 2''': For each disk <math>D_i</math> in the first stratum, there must exists a sequence <math>D_{i1}, D_{i2}, D_{i3}, \ldots</math> of disks in <math>X</math> such that for every <math>D_i</math>: <math display=block>D_{ij} \subseteq \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) D_i \quad \text{ for every } j</math> and <math>\cup_{j \in \N} D_{ij}</math> [[Absorbing set|absorbs]] <math>D_i.</math> The sets <math>\left(D_{ij}\right)_{i,j \in \N}</math> will form the second stratum. 
# '''Stratum 3''': To each disk <math>D_{ij}</math> in the second stratum, assign another sequence <math>D_{ij1}, D_{ij2}, D_{ij3}, \ldots</math> of disks in <math>X</math> satisfying analogously defined properties; explicitly, this means that for every <math>D_{i,j}</math>: <math display=block>D_{ijk} \subseteq \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) D_{ij} \quad \text{ for every } k</math> and <math>\cup_{k \in \N} D_{ijk}</math> [[Absorbing set|absorbs]] <math>D_{ij}.</math> The sets <math>\left(D_{ijk}\right)_{i,j,k \in \N}</math> form the third stratum. 

Continue this process to define strata <math>4, 5, \ldots.</math> That is, use induction to define stratum <math>n + 1</math> in terms of stratum <math>n.</math> 

A '''{{em|{{visible anchor|strand}}}}''' is a sequence of disks, with the first disk being selected from the first stratum, say <math>D_i,</math> and the second being selected from the sequence that was associated with <math>D_i,</math> and so on. We also require that if a sequence of vectors <math>(x_n)</math> is selected from a strand (with <math>x_1</math> belonging to the first disk in the strand, <math>x_2</math> belonging to the second, and so on) then the series <math>\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty} x_n</math> converges.

A [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[locally convex topological vector space]] on which a web can be defined is called a '''{{em|{{visible anchor|webbed space}}}}'''.

==Examples and sufficient conditions==

{{Math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=472}}|note=de Wilde 1978|math_statement=
A [[topological vector space]] <math>X</math> is a [[Fréchet space]] if and only if it is both a webbed space and a [[Baire space]].
}}

All of the following spaces are webbed:
* [[Fréchet space]]s.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=472}} 
* [[Projective limit]]s and [[inductive limit]]s of sequences of webbed spaces.
* A sequentially closed vector subspace of a webbed space.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=481}}
* Countable [[Product space|product]]s of webbed spaces.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=481}}
* A Hausdorff quotient of a webbed space.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=481}}
* The image of a webbed space under a [[sequentially continuous]] linear map if that image is [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]].{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=481}}
* The [[Bornological space|bornologification]] of a webbed space.
* The continuous dual space of a metrizable locally convex space endowed with the [[Strong dual space|strong dual topology]] is webbed.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=472}} 
* If <math>X</math> is the [[strict inductive limit]] of a denumerable family of locally convex metrizable spaces, then the [[continuous dual space]] of <math>X</math> with the [[Strong dual space|strong topology]] is webbed.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=473}} 
** So in particular, the [[Strong dual space|strong duals]] of locally convex [[Metrizable topological vector space|metrizable space]]s are webbed.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=459-483}}
* If <math>X</math> is a webbed space, then any Hausdorff locally convex topology weaker than this (webbed) topology is also webbed.{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|p=481}}

==Theorems==

{{Math theorem|name=Closed Graph Theorem{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=474-476}}|math_statement=
Let <math>A : X \to Y</math> be a linear map between TVSs that is [[sequentially closed]] (meaning that its graph is a sequentially closed subset of <math>X \times Y</math>). 
If <math>Y</math> is a webbed space and <math>X</math> is an [[ultrabornological space]] (such as a [[Fréchet space]] or an inductive limit of Fréchet spaces), then <math>A</math> is continuous.
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Closed Graph Theorem|math_statement=
Any closed linear map from the inductive limit of [[Baire space|Baire]] [[Locally convex topological vector space|locally convex space]]s into a webbed locally convex space is continuous.
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Open Mapping Theorem|math_statement=
Any continuous surjective linear map from a webbed locally convex space onto an [[inductive limit]] of Baire locally convex spaces is open.
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Open Mapping Theorem{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=474-476}}|math_statement=
Any continuous surjective linear map from a webbed locally convex space onto an [[ultrabornological space]] is open.
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Open Mapping Theorem{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=474-476}}|math_statement=
If the image of a closed linear operator <math>A : X \to Y</math> from locally convex webbed space <math>X</math> into Hausdorff locally convex space <math>Y</math> is [[Meagre set|nonmeager]] in <math>Y</math> then <math>A : X \to Y</math> is a surjective open map.
}}

If the spaces are not locally convex, then there is a notion of web where the requirement of being a disk is replaced by the requirement of being [[Balanced set|balanced]]. For such a notion of web we have the following results:

{{Math theorem|name=Closed Graph Theorem|math_statement=
Any closed linear map from the inductive limit of [[Baire space|Baire]] topological vector spaces into a webbed topological vector space is continuous.
}}
